C1.title: Sieve Echo Law H = α·log ω + β (§2.2)
C1.reason: H_paper: test R² law-only 0.190, baseline (log L, log n) 0.925, full 0.925; ΔR² 0.0001 CI [-0.001, 0.001] (threshold 0.01); partial r(H, log ω | log L, log n) -0.048.

C2.title: Direction of the effect (§1.3, §7.1)
C2.reason: Measured on test (H_paper): primes minus composites mean H = 0.419 CI [0.358, 0.478]; Spearman(H, ω) -0.476 (negative); given log L and log n the sign is negative. Primes have the highest entropy, so §1.3 ('primes low-entropy') and §7.1 item 2 are contradicted; only α < 0 holds.

C3.title: Prime-power dichotomy (§2.3)
C3.reason: The paper's -0.843 is corr(ω, is_prime_power) (v11: -0.655 on [2, 9999]), not an entropy correlation. Actual r(H, prime power) on test = 0.309 (positive: prime powers have higher H); given log L, log n: -0.082 CI [-0.131, -0.034].

C4.title: Base invariance CV < 0.1 (§2.4, Q5.2)
C4.reason: v8.2's 6% is a 100-integer sample (v11 on all n in [2, 9999]: 0.091). Spearman(CV, log n) for v8/H_paper: -0.022 CI [-0.038, -0.001]. Highest overall rate: v8/Hn_nodc = 0.930. Normalized DC-free entropy saturates near its maximum for long, noise-like repetends, so its CV shrinks with L; the CV of log L itself also falls with n.

C5.title: Correlation with n^-s (zeta, §4.1)
C5.reason: n^-s is a monotone function of n; after a cubic in log n the partial correlations are s=2: -0.030, s=3: -0.026, s=4: -0.023; H ~ log n alone has test R² 0.340.

C6.title: H·log n vs prime number theorem (§4.2)
C6.reason: corr(H·log n, H) = 0.946; with H randomly permuted across n the same statistic is 0.831 CI [0.826, 0.836]: most of it comes from H appearing on both sides, the rest from H growing with n (corr(H, log n) = 0.593). PNT/Li errors are functions of n; partial r given log n: pnt -0.033, li -0.031.

C7.title: Residue-class structure mod 6/12/30/210 (§4.3)
C7.verdict: supported (residue structure beyond per-base L and ω)
C7.reason: η² of residue class on test, raw → excess over the permutation null after controls. H_paper: mod 6: 0.209 → excess 0.005 (p 0.030), mod 12: 0.233 → excess 0.052 (p 0.002), mod 30: 0.252 → excess 0.017 (p 0.002), mod 210: 0.374 → excess 0.034 (p 0.006). H_nodc: mod 6: 0.126 → excess -0.001 (p 0.611), mod 12: 0.157 → excess 0.032 (p 0.002), mod 30: 0.184 → excess 0.008 (p 0.086), mod 210: 0.328 → excess 0.026 (p 0.026). Residues mod 6/12/30/210 fix divisibility by 2, 3, 5, 7 and the quadratic characters of the bases, which set the per-base orders.

C8.title: Fitted constants vs theory and constant matching (§5)
C8.reason: Theory constants inside a 95% CI: no. A value drawn at random near α matches some library combination within 0.01 with probability 0.87 (near β: 0.88), so the matches carry no evidence; α and β also change with log(ω) vs log(ω+1) and with the entropy definition.

C9.title: Information about ω beyond L and n (core question)
C9.reason: Held-out ω classification: baseline (n, per-base L, lcm arithmetic) accuracy 0.978; +entropy features 0.980 (Δ +0.003 CI [-0.003, 0.009]); +all NDR features 0.986 (Δ +0.008 CI [0.003, 0.015], log-loss gain +0.0210 CI [0.006, 0.038]); majority 0.399, shuffled-label null 0.368.
